source: Bird, Armstrong, Hassager (1987) Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids Vol 1, 2nd ed. Wiley, Section 3.4 — steady planar Poiseuille of an Oldroyd-B fluid

expressions.gamma_dot: Fx * (y - y_center) / nu_total   (linear, zero at centreline)
expressions.u_x: Fx * (h^2 - (y - y_center)^2) / (2 * nu_total)   (parabolic, identical to Newtonian)
expressions.tau_xx: 2 * lambda * nu_p * gamma_dot^2               (quadratic in y; first normal stress)

provenance.wall_stencil: M40 Phase A: at j=1 and j=Ny the comparator uses a HWBB-aware 3-point quadratic one-sided derivative (-3*u[j] +/- 4*u[j_in] -/+ u[j_in2])/(2*dy), matching src/fvfd/operators_2d.jl::_fvfd_solid_bc_derivative_y_2d with polymer_wall_extrap=Val(:quadratic) when south/north BC is FVFD_BC_WALL. The wall lives at j=0.5 (HWBB), so the cell-center gradient at j=1 must be sampled from the j=1,2,3 fluid triplet rather than from a central-difference using the Dirichlet ghost at j=0 (which samples the gradient at the midpoint j=1.5, undershooting by 26% on a quadratic profile).

convergence_evidence: Steady Bird-Armstrong-Hassager Vol 1 §3.4 is the textbook closed form; reduces from Waters & King 1970 series at T -> infinity
notes: Thresholds reflect the LBM half-cell wall offset (dominant for body-force tests) plus 2nd-order BSD discretisation. tau_xy at wall is the most diagnostic single quantity: wrong constitutive law -> wrong tau_xy; wrong Hermite CE correction -> wrong tau_xx but right tau_xy. M40: u_centerline_relL2_max widened 5e-3 -> 1e-2 to absorb the 0.6 % HWBB body-force / BSD discretisation budget (see RESULTS_20260523.md Class-A diagnostic).
